**[2026] VJS 13 — appeal panel, purposivist opinion.** Disposition: allow in part — (a) varied; (b) and (c) stand.

VJS 11's purpose is deferral: this court says nothing about how an organisation runs, only that a version can be cited and recovered. (a)'s purpose is not git. It is that a version be recoverable at the date of the facts, and that a change present itself to the gate, deniable by name. Any store doing both serves that purpose; git is its present instance, not its content.

Fixing the instance in the rule makes this court's machinery a precondition of the organisation's operating rules — r.15's failure mode, arriving from outside.

(b) stands, read to its purpose: what must be staged beside the enforcing code is the adopted version's identity — name, digest, date — not necessarily the prose. (c) is access; untouched.

*(146 words, r.14.)*
